title: exagium: one queue after the whole-project audit (2026-11-17)
intro: Built from six skill-group audits (A security, B tests/bugs/state, C structure, D claims, E agents/free compute, F ML/binaries), a separate verification pass (S2: 15 of 16 high-impact items confirmed by reproduction, 1 partly right), and the 2026-11-13 audit and handoffs. items.title: Hypothesis (owner, 2026-11-18): the cheapest artifact is the one whose structure is the process the hardware already runs (fewer translation layers between model and native primitives = lower cost at equal accuracy)
items.next: Fold into the transfer test / mixed suite (forge-next-item-2026-11-18 steps 1-2) rather than a separate build: add native-primitive families next to the float ones (lookup tables and constraint propagation first, as the cheapest to port; then Tsetlin, cellular automata, event-driven). Fix before running: supported if their cost lead at matched accuracy holds on at least 2 non-digit tasks; weakened if it holds only on digits/perception or vanishes once accuracy is matched. Offload: once the free proposer exists, give it this as a hypothesis to generate candidates for; Claude only checks. Evidence so far, digits only: LGN 0.45x instructions, 1.9-3.3x cheaper per image at large N, -0.7 pt dev accuracy; staging page faults were ~1/3 of mlp16's time. Update 2026-11-18 (P1, transfer/results/2026-11-18/): for the gate network, the digits-only lead did not carry over: on text and UCI Adult it used 2.1x and 1.3x mlp16's instructions and was less accurate, so on the first two non-digit tasks this family weakens the hypothesis (sizes grew with the class count: 50 output gates per class). Lookup-table and constraint-propagation families are still untested; add them in P3.

items.title: Queue worker: free models keep working the queue without a chat (claims, leases, automatic notes and handoffs)
items.next: Owner, 2026-11-18: work should continue when the chat or Claude's limit stops. Design (hypothesis): git as the coordinator: each item gets claimed_by and lease_until; a worker claims by committing to queue.json, and git rejects a second concurrent push, so no double-ups; an expired lease frees the item. A scheduled Actions job picks the top ready item whose tier allows a free model, claims it, does it (key and generated code in separate jobs, as P5), writes the result, a run note and the new status, and releases. Trust tiers from data (bench-2 Nemotron 3/3, bench-5 NIM 11/15: good, not unchecked): docs/mechanical (B5, B4) may self-merge after a script confirms only targeted lines changed and a second free model reviews; code goes to a PR with tests and free review, final check by Claude or the owner; design stays with Claude. A daily digest drafts the handoff and README update, flagging any number without an openable artifact. P5 (proposer) becomes one job type of this worker. Cheapest test: B5 docs items, two workers at once to force claim races; measure double claims (target 0), share of free drafts accepted on spot check, stuck leases. Limits and pacing (owner, 2026-11-18): a budget ledger per pool and period (minute, day, month, $), seeded from measured limits: Actions free and unlimited on this public repo, 20 concurrent jobs (GitHub docs); OpenRouter 1,000 req/day; Groq 1,000 req/day and 8,000 tokens/min (headers, run 44197136667); Cloudflare 10k neurons/day; NIM shape unmeasured (about 30/min for 10 min, then 3-5/min refusals, bench-5); Cerebras/xAI/Gemini in $ via P4. A run reserves budget by commit before calling (same CAS as claims); live remaining-quota headers override the seed; a 429 marks the pool exhausted until its window resets; the daily budget is spread across runs with ~10% kept for probes and reviews; unknown shapes (NIM) become low-priority measurement jobs; each job takes the cheapest pool measured good enough for its kind of work with budget left, else CPU-only work or a clean stop with the reason recorded. Builds on P4 (spend caps) and Q22 (usage log). Coexisting with chat sessions (owner, 2026-11-18): the worker never calls Claude, so chats never draw on its budget and it never draws on the owner's Claude limit. Shared resources get rules: chats claim items like workers (claimed_by chat-<session>) and a chat claim wins; the worker skips any batch that touches the same paths; each free pool keeps a reserved share (start at 20%) for chat-started reviews; the worker caps itself at about half of Actions' 20 concurrent jobs; it commits only to its own branches/PRs (plus claim commits); a repo variable the owner can flip pauses new claims.

items.title: Process manager: measure, watch and improve how the free workers work (no worker changes its own rules)
items.next: Owner, 2026-11-18: with free workers doing routine work, Claude's role becomes managing the process. Split by part: measure by script every run (valid rate, spot-check acceptance, claim conflicts, budget used vs wasted, time per item, reverts, cost per accepted item per pool); spot problems weekly with a free model reading metrics and run notes; it files proposals as queue items of kind 'process' with evidence; Claude decides and redesigns periodically in an owner-opened chat (free reviewers' points were only partly usable: 3 of 8 applied in bench-5); changes audited by a reviewer of another model family. Rules: no worker changes its own rules (process changes go through the queue); the manager's own proposals are scored by whether they moved the numbers they targeted. Define the metrics from P8's first runs, not before.

items.title: Whole-system auditor: an independent, periodic look at direction, debt and blind spots that can't be seen from inside a task
items.next: Indicator script and baseline done (main d4d5e8d, audit/periodic/; free review applied 6, rejected 5 with evidence). Remaining: (1) weekly workflow running indicators.py with --previous, posting a GitHub issue to the owner (waits on Q07); (2) direction check by a free model of another family, reading churn_7d and completed queue items against the README's purpose (baseline: about 1/5 of 7-day code churn in runner/transfer/tasks); (3) deferred indicators: test coverage, lint warnings, dependency freshness (need tools installed); (4) monthly deep audit by Claude agents or on a tripped indicator. Owner, 2026-11-18: something whose only job is to look at the whole: wrong direction, accruing debt, anything invisible locally. Evidence it pays: the 2026-11-17 audit found 52 items; S2 confirmed 15 of 16 high-impact ones by reproduction (router probe red 12 of 12, loop CI unable to fail, a bench grade-step escape), none visible from inside the tasks that made them; it cost 6 parallel Claude agents plus verification. Tiers: weekly indicators by script on CI (size and duplication, dead files, tests that can't fail, CI red rate, queue item age, stale branches, claims without evidence); weekly direction check by free models in fresh context, of another family than the builders, comparing completed work with the README's 'What this is for'; deep audit by Claude agents monthly or when an indicator trips. Rules: reports straight to the owner, not via Claude or the process manager; read-only; fresh context; its findings are scored by whether they checked out, which sets how often the expensive tier runs. The indicator script needs no worker and can start first; its workflow waits on Q07.
